blocks.text: 8. General Operations and Configurations
8.1 Switching on and off
The power button of the BactoSense is located on the right hand-side of the instrument.
blocks.html: The power button of the BactoSense is located on the right hand-side of the instrument.

blocks.text: Original manual illustration, printed page 58
Figure 8-1 Power button of the BactoSense
blocks.html: Figure 8-1 Power button of the BactoSense

blocks.text: Check the power supply Before switching the BactoSense on, make sure that the instrument is connected to a stable power supply meeting the requirements described in Connecting the BactoSense to power .
blocks.html:
CHECK THE POWER SUPPLY

Before switching the BactoSense on, make sure that the instrument is connected to a stable power supply meeting the requirements described in Connecting the BactoSense to power.

blocks.text: Switching on To switch the BactoSense on, shortly press on the power button. The power button LED lights up constantly and after a few seconds, the welcome screen is displayed on the user interface.
blocks.html: Switching on To switch the BactoSense on, shortly press on the power button. The power button LED lights up constantly and after a few seconds, the welcome screen is displayed on the user interface.

blocks.text: Switching off If you are logged in and want to switch the BactoSense off, tap on the logout button on the top right corner of the user interface and select Power off . If you want to switch off from the login page itself, press the power button for 10 seconds.
blocks.html: Switching off If you are logged in and want to switch the BactoSense off, tap on the logout button on the top right corner of the user interface and select Power off. If you want to switch off from the login page itself, press the power button for 10 seconds.

blocks.text: Disconnect power safely To disconnect the BactoSense from power, first switch the instrument off. Then unplug the power supply unit from the mains power source, before unplugging the power supply plug from the BactoSense.
blocks.html:
DISCONNECT POWER SAFELY

To disconnect the BactoSense from power, first switch the instrument off. Then unplug the power supply unit from the mains power source, before unplugging the power supply plug from the BactoSense.

blocks.text: 8.2 Login, user roles and permissions

BactoSense operation requires users to log in. Different user roles with different permissions are available. The user role permissions are listed in User roles and permissions . All logins are password protected.
blocks.html: BactoSense operation requires users to log in. Different user roles with different permissions are available. The user role permissions are listed in User roles and permissions. All logins are password protected.

blocks.text: Login and logout can be performed using the login button displayed in the top right corner of the user interface. The currently active user role is displayed next to that button.
blocks.html: Login and logout can be performed using the login button displayed in the top right corner of the user interface. The currently active user role is displayed next to that button.

blocks.text: 8.2.1 Login

WORK STEP 1. Press the login button on the top right corner of the user interface, or the login bar at the bottom in case you switched on the instrument. 2. For BactoSense CORE or BactoSense ID in the standard configuration: Select one of the user profiles Basic, Advanced or Admin. For BactoSense CORE or BactoSense ID upgraded with the Management package (see Management package ) and advanced user management mode activated (see Activating advanced user management mode ), enter your user ID. 3. Enter the password and press OK. If you don’t know the password, ask your Admin user. In a new instrument no passwords are set. In that case, follow the procedure described in Setting and changing passwords . 4. After logging in, you see the BactoSense user interface. 5. To log out, follow the procedure described in Manual logout .
blocks.html:
WORK STEP
1.Press the login button on the top right corner of the user interface, or the login bar at the bottom in case you switched on the instrument.
2.For BactoSense CORE or BactoSense ID in the standard configuration: Select one of the user profiles Basic, Advanced or Admin. For BactoSense CORE or BactoSense ID upgraded with the Management package (see Management package) and advanced user management mode activated (see Activating advanced user management mode), enter your user ID.
3.Enter the password and press OK. If you don’t know the password, ask your Admin user. In a new instrument no passwords are set. In that case, follow the procedure described in Setting and changing passwords.
4.After logging in, you see the BactoSense user interface.
5.To log out, follow the procedure described in Manual logout.

blocks.text: 8.2.2 Manual logout

WORK STEP 1. Make sure all processes (e.g. measurements or cleanings) have completed. The idle state of the instrument is indicated on the left hand-side of the top bar of the BactoSense user interface. 2. Press the logout button in the top right corner of the user interface. 3. Select Log out / Lock screen. 4. To log in again, follow the procedure described in Login .
blocks.html:
WORK STEP
1.Make sure all processes (e.g. measurements or cleanings) have completed. The idle state of the instrument is indicated on the left hand-side of the top bar of the BactoSense user interface.
2.Press the logout button in the top right corner of the user interface.
3.Select Log out / Lock screen.
4.To log in again, follow the procedure described in Login.

blocks.text: 8.2.3 Auto-logout
It is possible to configure an automated logout after predefined period of inactivity.

blocks.text: WORK STEP ADDITIONAL INFO / IMAGE 1. As an Admin user, press Settings on the Home screen to open the settings menu. 2. Press the System settings button. 3. Press the Users button. 4. Press the Settings button. 5. Configure the desired auto-logout time period. 6. Press Save.

blocks.text: 8.2.4 Activating advanced user management mode

With the Advanced User Management feature, an instrument admin can create different users and assign different user roles (Basic, Advanced, Admin). This allows to give different permissions to individual users, and log their activity for the audit trail.

The BactoSense has a built-in auto-restart functionality to automatically recover from temporary power interruptions. Depending on the configuration, the instrument can simply restart, but also return to operation by performing a self-cleaning process and restarting an Online mode series.

Depending on the configuration, the instrument can simply restart, but also return to operation by performing a self-cleaning process and restarting an Online mode series.

blocks.text: 8.4 Import / export settings

Settings are exported to a USB drive as per Export settings, diagnostics, or all to USB device . The settings are compiled to a timestamped file ending with * .bnv . In order to import the settings in a new instrument, or as a backup, it is necessary to copy the * .bnv file at the root of the USB drive, or in the directory the file was exported to. If multiple copies of the settings are located in one USB drive, the system will use the most recent one.
blocks.html: Settings are exported to a USB drive as per Export settings, diagnostics, or all to USB device. The settings are compiled to a timestamped file ending with *.bnv. In order to import the settings in a new instrument, or as a backup, it is necessary to copy the *.bnv file at the root of the USB drive, or in the directory the file was exported to. If multiple copies of the settings are located in one USB drive, the system will use the most recent one.

blocks.text: WORK STEP ADDITIONAL INFO / IMAGE 1. As an Admin user, press Settings on the Home screen to open the settings menu. 2. Press the Maintenance button. 3. Press the Special export import button. 4. Connect a USB drive. If needed, press the Refresh USB list button until the drive is detected. Make sure the *.bnv file is at the root of the USB drive. The USB drive should be formatted in FAT32, which is the common standard. 5. Press the Import settings button. 6. Select the settings you want to import. Measurement settings include gate sets, IO settings, alarms, and date and time settings. Network settings include IP, DNS, and NTP addresses 7. Press Import settings, then Reboot now in the confirmation message, and wait until the device reboots.
blocks.html:
WORK STEPADDITIONAL INFO / IMAGE
1.As an Admin user, press Settings on the Home screen to open the settings menu.
2.Press the Maintenance button.
3.Press the Special export import button.
4.Connect a USB drive. If needed, press the Refresh USB list button until the drive is detected.Make sure the *.bnv file is at the root of the USB drive. The USB drive should be formatted in FAT32, which is the common standard.
5.Press the Import settings button.
6.Select the settings you want to import. Measurement settings include gate sets, IO settings, alarms, and date and time settings. Network settings include IP, DNS, and NTP addresses
7.Press Import settings, then Reboot now in the confirmation message, and wait until the device reboots.

blocks.text: 8.7 Set NTP Servers

blocks.text: 8.9 Cartridge management

The BactoSense cartridges contain the reagents required for measuring and maintaining the instrument clean. Available cartridge types are TCC (Total Cell Count), ICC (Intact Cell Count), EBC (E. coli Cell Count), ACC (Active Cell Count), CBC (Coliform Cell Count), and NBC (Enterococcus Cell Count). The following sections explain cartridge handling. Cartridge storage, transportation and refill are described in Storage, Transport and Disposal .
blocks.html: The BactoSense cartridges contain the reagents required for measuring and maintaining the instrument clean. Available cartridge types are TCC (Total Cell Count), ICC (Intact Cell Count), EBC (E. coli Cell Count), ACC (Active Cell Count), CBC (Coliform Cell Count), and NBC (Enterococcus Cell Count). The following sections explain cartridge handling. Cartridge storage, transportation and refill are described in Storage, Transport and Disposal.

blocks.text: 8.9.1 General instructions for cartridge handling
When handling the cartridge, the following instructions must be followed:
blocks.html: When handling the cartridge, the following instructions must be followed:

blocks.text: Table 8-3 Cartridge handling instructions

The cartridge filling levels and expiration date can be retrieved from several sources.

blocks.text: 8.10 Switching between sampling devices

The BactoSense can be operated with either the manual or the online sampling device. The following procedure describes the exchange of sampling devices. Sampling device storage information can be found in Storage of the sampling devices .

blocks.text: 8.10.1 Removal of the online sampling device
When switching to the manual sampling device, the online sampling device has to be removed. Follow the procedure below to safely remove the device and prepare it for storage.
blocks.html: When switching to the manual sampling device, the online sampling device has to be removed. Follow the procedure below to safely remove the device and prepare it for storage.

blocks.text: Wear protective gloves Avoid contamination of the equipment. Wear nitrile gloves when handling samples, sampling devices and any components which come in contact with them.
blocks.html:
WEAR PROTECTIVE GLOVES

Avoid contamination of the equipment. Wear nitrile gloves when handling samples, sampling devices and any components which come in contact with them.

blocks.text: WORK STEP 1. Terminate any ongoing measurement series, as described in Terminating automatic online measurements . 2. Stop the water flow through the sampling device tubings and sampling device. 3. Carefully unscrew the knurled sampling device fixation ring until the sampling device can be removed. 4. Remove the online sampling device. Make sure the white sealing plug still sits tightly in the connector of the sampling device. If not, it may have remained in the BactoSense sampling device connector. In this case carefully remove it with tweezers and place it back in the sampling device. 5. Disconnect and drain the inlet and outlet tubings from the water source and the sampling device body. 6. Inspect the inlet and outlet tubings for contamination and damage. Only reuse clean and intact tubings. 7. If you want to store the sampling device, place the device and the tubings separately in a clean and dry plastic bags and follow the storage instructions in Storage of the sampling devices . 8. To mount now the manual sampling device, see Installation of the manual sampling device .

blocks.text: 8.11 Qualification
Qualification is a process to ensure the BactoSense operates as intended. Different options are available.

blocks.text: To do a fully automated quick check of the instrument status, perform the self-check procedure described in Automatic self-check . This test does not require any reagents or user interaction, is very quick and checks the integrity and communication between the different modules of the BactoSense.

blocks.text: For operational environments requiring system suitability testing, use the System Suitability Test Kit (SST Kit) and follow the procedure in its user manual.

blocks.text: 8.11.1 Cleanliness verification

WORK STEP 1. Make sure the manual sampling device is tightly installed as described in Installation of the manual sampling device . 2. Perform a cleaning of the sampling device with two replications: If a Washstation is available, follow the procedure in Clean manual sampling device with Washstation , otherwise the procedure in Clean manual sampling device with basic cleaning . 3. Prepare the blank sample in a 5 mL screw-cap tube. There are two options: A) Use cell-free water, e.g. a sterile solution aliquot from the Validation Kit. If you use the sterile solution aliquot from the Validation Kit, remove the cap of the aliquot and place the aliquot in an empty 5 mL screw-cap tube, as described in the user manual of the Validation Kit. B) Take a still mineral water and filter twice using a membrane filter with a pore size of 0.22 µm or smaller. 4. Navigate to the Home screen of the BactoSense user interface. 5. On the Home screen, press Mode and select Manual mode. Press Back, then Measure to open the measurement wizard. 6. Select Prime from the list of available protocols. 7. Press the Next button. 8. Remove the tube or Washstation from the manual sampling device and attach the blank sample. 9. Press the Start button to run the Prime protocol. 10. After completion of the Prime, press the New button to navigate back to the list of protocols. 11. Select Water Analysis from the list of available protocols. 12. Configure two replications. 13. Enter a sample name by tapping into the Sample name text field, entering the name and pressing OK. 14. Verify that the ICC or TCC default gate is configured and change it otherwise by pressing into the Gates field. 15. Press the Next button. 16. Press the Start button and wait for the two measurements to complete. 17. After finishing, press the Next button to review the results. 18. Look at the results and compare them to the reference values indicated below. The BactoSense is clean if the following criteria are fulfilled: • For TCC cartridges: TCC [/mL] < 300 • For ICC cartridges: ICC [/mL] < 100 19. If the cell concentrations are higher than the specified limits, apply the following procedure: • Repeat the procedure with a freshly prepared blank sample. • Repeat the procedure after a decontamination using the Cleaning Kit (see Consumables ). • If the test keeps failing, contact bNovate support or your local service representative. 20. After finishing, attach a clean and empty 5 mL screw-cap tube or the Washstation to the manual sampling device.

WORK STEP
1.Make sure the manual sampling device is tightly installed as described in Installation of the manual sampling device.
2.Perform a cleaning of the sampling device with two replications: If a Washstation is available, follow the procedure in Clean manual sampling device with Washstation, otherwise the procedure in Clean manual sampling device with basic cleaning.
3.Prepare the blank sample in a 5 mL screw-cap tube. There are two options: A) Use cell-free water, e.g. a sterile solution aliquot from the Validation Kit. If you use the sterile solution aliquot from the Validation Kit, remove the cap of the aliquot and place the aliquot in an empty 5 mL screw-cap tube, as described in the user manual of the Validation Kit. B) Take a still mineral water and filter twice using a membrane filter with a pore size of 0.22 µm or smaller.
4.Navigate to the Home screen of the BactoSense user interface.
5.On the Home screen, press Mode and select Manual mode. Press Back, then Measure to open the measurement wizard.
6.Select Prime from the list of available protocols.
7.Press the Next button.
8.Remove the tube or Washstation from the manual sampling device and attach the blank sample.
9.Press the Start button to run the Prime protocol.
10.After completion of the Prime, press the New button to navigate back to the list of protocols.
11.Select Water Analysis from the list of available protocols.
12.Configure two replications.
13.Enter a sample name by tapping into the Sample name text field, entering the name and pressing OK.
14.Verify that the ICC or TCC default gate is configured and change it otherwise by pressing into the Gates field.
15.Press the Next button.
16.Press the Start button and wait for the two measurements to complete.
17.After finishing, press the Next button to review the results.
18.Look at the results and compare them to the reference values indicated below. The BactoSense is clean if the following criteria are fulfilled: • For TCC cartridges: TCC [/mL] < 300 • For ICC cartridges: ICC [/mL] < 100
19.If the cell concentrations are higher than the specified limits, apply the following procedure: • Repeat the procedure with a freshly prepared blank sample. • Repeat the procedure after a decontamination using the Cleaning Kit (see Consumables). • If the test keeps failing, contact bNovate support or your local service representative.
20.After finishing, attach a clean and empty 5 mL screw-cap tube or the Washstation to the manual sampling device.

blocks.text: 8.12 Demo mode

Demo mode can be used when demonstrating the device or when learning how to navigate the menus and use the functions. When it is activated, the instrument reboots into a special mode that displays demonstration data (the owner’s measurement results are hidden). All the instrument’s functions are replaced by simulations that never move the hardware or modify the results database. This means protocols can be started without needing to load a sample, and users can pretend to delete or re-gate results without ever changing the data. If the demo mode is activated, the message Demo is displayed in the upper middle of the screen. When the instrument is reverted to normal mode, the owner’s data is shown again, and all functions are active again.
